## Cognitive Screening & Clinical Decision-Making

Today's simulation focuses on cognitive-communication screening, clinical readiness, and functional implications following right hemisphere stroke.

Students will review medical and interdisciplinary documentation, determine the appropriateness of cognitive screening, administer the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), and interpret findings in the context of functional communication, safety, and discharge planning.
:::

::: {.warning}
## SLP Task

You have received a consult for a cognitive-communication evaluation for Cindy Carlson, a 92-year-old female admitted following a right MCA ischemic stroke.

Review the available clinical information to determine whether cognitive screening is appropriate at this time.

If appropriate, administer the MoCA and use your findings to identify areas of cognitive-communication concern, discuss functional implications, and develop recommendations.

Throughout the session, consider how medical status, environmental factors, and patient presentation may influence assessment and interpretation.
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, students will be able to:

- Identify cognitive-communication deficits commonly associated with right hemisphere stroke.
- Gather relevant information from medical and interdisciplinary documentation.
- Evaluate patient readiness for cognitive screening based on medical, cognitive, and behavioral factors.
- Demonstrate appropriate administration of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).
- Interpret screening findings while recognizing the limitations of standardized cognitive screening.
- Connect cognitive-communication findings to functional activities, safety, and discharge planning.
- Communicate findings and recommendations using professional, patient-centered language.

---

## Today's Modules

### 1. Medical Chart Review

Review Cindy Carlson's medical history, admitting diagnosis, neuroimaging, medications, prior level of function, and current plan of care.

Identify relevant risk factors and consider how her neurological presentation may influence cognitive-communication functioning.

[Begin Chart Review](chart.html)

### 2. Interdisciplinary Documentation

Review documentation from nursing, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and the medical team.

Identify observations that may suggest cognitive-communication impairment and consider how interdisciplinary findings contribute to your assessment plan.

[Review Interdisciplinary Notes](interdisciplinary.html)

### 3. Cognitive Screening Readiness

Evaluate Cindy's current medical status, alertness, communication abilities, and participation to determine whether cognitive screening is appropriate.

Discuss factors that may influence the validity of MoCA administration and identify potential modifications or reasons to defer screening.

[Assess Screening Readiness](readiness.html)

### 4. Cognitive Screening & Functional Implications

Administer the MoCA during the simulation, as appropriate.

Interpret findings across cognitive domains and discuss how identified strengths and weaknesses may influence functional independence, safety awareness, and discharge planning.

Consider the limitations of screening results and whether additional assessment is warranted.

[Explore Functional Implications](implications.html)
